newsitem.title: USA: Researchers find possible key to Gehrig's disease.
newsitem.headline: Researchers find possible key to Gehrig's disease.

text.p: Researchers may have found a key to unlocking the deadly mysteries of Lou Gehrig's disease, the journal Science reported on Thursday.

The ailment, formally known as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, is a rare, fatal degenerative disease that weakens and fatally paralyses its victims. Its most famous sufferer was New York Yankee great Lou Gehrig, who died in 1941.

Scientists in the United States and Switzerland found that mice with symptoms of the disease could live longer if they were made to produce over-abundant amounts of a specific protein that deals with the death of cells in the body.

The overproduction of this protein, known as bcl-2, did not alter the course of the disease, and the mice eventually died. But researchers suggested that therapies that interfere with cell death could improve the quality of life for patients with this disease.
